newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Vereinsbank, HypoBank to merge. [CORRECTED 11:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Vereinsbank, HypoBank to merge. [CORRECTED 11:55 GMT]

text.p: Germany's fourth and fifth largest banks on Monday announced plans to merge, creating a new number-two player in the German market that will rival market leader Deutsche Bank AG.

Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechselbank AG, the number four and five respectively among listed commercial banks, said they were joining forces to form Bayerische Hypo- und Vereinsbank AG.
The new bank will have combined assets of 743 billion marks ($415 billion), outranking Dresdner Bank AG and not far off Deutsche, whose total assets in 1996 were 886 billion marks.

Germany's heavily overbanked market has been ripe for a merger, with the "Bavarian solution" presented in Monday's announcement seen as one of the most likely scenarios for much-needed consolidation in the sector.
Edmund (correcting first name) Stoiber, prime minister in the powerful southern state of Bavaria, welcomed the merger plans, saying they would strengthen the competitiveness of the two banks.

In the first step of a two-stage merger plan, shareholders in Hypo-Bank will be offered shares in insurer Allianz AG at a rate of one Allianz share per six Hypo-Bank shares held, equating to a price of around 75 marks per share.

This would give Vereinsbank a stake of up to 45 percent in Hypo-Bank, with the Allianz shares involved coming from Vereinsbank's portfolio. An official offer document would be published next week, Vereinsbank said.
In a second stage, the full merger of the two banks would be prepared from October, with plans presented to shareholders for approval by spring 1998 at the latest.
Allianz is a shareholder in both banks and will hold 15 percent of the new merged bank, which it said would allow it to use the network for insurance and assets products.

Bank shares in general surged on the Frankfurt bourse when computer trading opened. Vereinsbank shares jumped 12.2 percent to 92 marks while Hypo-Bank stock jumped 25 percent to trade just under the 75-mark offer price at 73 marks.

But analysts' initial reactions were mixed. Commerzbank immediately raised its recommendation on the top five listed German banking stocks to a "buy", while Salomon reduced its recommendation on Vereinsbank to "hold" from "buy".

The German cartel office, which will have to give its go-ahead to the merger, said preliminary talks had already been held but that it had not yet received official notification of the merger plan. This was expected in the next few days.
Expectations that the financial services sector was on the brink of a shake-up gained fresh currency in recent weeks after news of a merger of two insurers under Munich Re.
Munich Re said it would merge its two affiliates Victoria Holding AG and Hamburg-Mannheimer AG to form Germany's second largest primary insurer after Allianz AG.
"When things start to happen in the insurance sector the speculation spills over into bank stocks," Stefan Ermisch, banking analyst at Westdeutsche Landesbank said last week.

The rationale behind mergers is clear. Germany is regarded as heavily overbanked with more than 3,600 commercial, public and cooperative banks battling for market share, and a rate of one branch per 1,100 inhabitants.
The top five banks, led by Deutsche, have a joint market share of just 14 percent and are struggling to make their costly retail branch networks more efficient.

The Bavarian banks said the merger would cost around 1.3 billion marks in restructuring costs. But it also promised cost cuts of as much as one billion marks per year and said the joint group would have "markedly higher" earnings per share.
Sources said the two banks could cut between 5,000 and 7,000 jobs over the next five years.
Other major corporates responded cautiously to the news.

Dresdner Bank AG the current number-two bank in Germany, which could have merged with Hypo-Bank under one of the alternative scenarios, said in a statement that it did not expect the merger to disrupt its strategic links to Allianz.

Deutsche, which holds 5.21 percent of Vereinsbank, gave a cautious welcome to the plans, terming its stake in Vereinsbank "a good investment". Viag, which indirectly owns 10.24 percent of Vereinsbank, said it would retain its stake in the bank.
--Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
($ = 1.787 German Marks)
